title: A needle for the next world
told: a sakhi of Guru Nanak, a traditional story

hook.say: before the story, can i ask you something? if you had to leave home today and take only one thing, what would you grab?
options: that’s the question in this story. listen.

steps.line: In Lahore lived a very rich man named Duni Chand. Over his house flew flags, one for every hundred thousand rupees he owned.
steps.label: a traditional story

steps.line: When Guru Nanak came to visit, Duni Chand showed him everything, and asked: is there anything I can do for you?
The Guru handed him a small sewing needle. Keep this for me, he said. Give it back to me in the next world.

steps.q: Duni Chand puts the needle away safely. Who do you think sees the problem with it?
steps.why: His wife: how does a needle go with you past death? The Guru Granth Sahib says it again and again: wealth stays behind; it doesn’t go along with you.

steps.line: His wife asked: how will you take a needle with you when you die? Nobody can take anything.
Duni Chand ran back. I can’t carry even a needle, he said. Then how will all your fortune go with you? the Guru asked.

steps.q: After the needle, why would Duni Chand start giving instead of adding another flag?
o: He wanted the Guru to praise him
Wealth can only do good while you live
He feared thieves would take it all
steps.why: Nothing goes with you. So the only time wealth can feed anyone is now.

steps.line: So Duni Chand began to share: food and money for the hungry, given with his own hands.
Sikhs call this vand chakna: share, then eat. Many set aside a tenth of what they earn for others, called dasvandh.
steps.label: today

steps.q: Many Sikhs give dasvandh, a tenth, to the gurdwara. What does the gurdwara famously do with much of it?
o: Feeds anyone who walks in, free
steps.why: The langar: a free kitchen where everyone sits on the floor as equals. The Golden Temple’s kitchen serves tens of thousands a day.

steps.q: Vand chakna puts sharing before eating. What changes when you share first, not from what’s left over?
o: Others get the first portion, not scraps
You end up eating less every day
It’s easier to keep count of
steps.why: What’s left over depends on your mood. The first portion is a decision, given before you take your own.

say: here’s what i love. the guru didn’t lecture duni chand. he handed him a needle, and let the question do the work.
that’s vand chakna, the next pillar: share first, then enjoy what’s yours. not what’s left over at the end. the first portion.

steps.q: The Guru could have asked for anything. From the story, why ask for something as small as a needle?
o: It was all he could carry on the road
If a needle can’t go, nothing can
Needles were rare and precious then
steps.why: The smaller the thing, the bigger the point. A sermon can be argued with; a needle just sits in your hand.

today.say: today, take the first portion of something, a slice, an hour, a little money, and give it before you enjoy the rest. that’s the order: share, then eat.
options: then enjoy the rest. you earned it.
then share a small thing. the needle was small too.

card.keepWhy: Nothing goes with you. So share it now.
